claim: Ehsani and Linnainmaa (JF 77(3) 2022; NBER w25551): most factors are positively autocorrelated; the average factor earns about 1 bp a month after a year of losses and 53 bp after a positive year. Table 3 (up to 20 factors, July 1964 onward, monthly): equal-weighted factors Sharpe 1.06, time-series winners (prior one-year return > 0) 1.33, losers 0.04, long-short time-series factor momentum 0.98, cross-sectional 0.76.
impact_on_spec: Defines the timing rule: sign of the prior one-year factor return, winners-only (FM12, FM12T) or tilted (FM12H); the long-short form is not tested because it underperforms equal weight in Table 3.
independent_replication: Gupta and Kelly (JPM 2019) and Arnott et al. report factor momentum on other factor sets; Fan et al. 2022 dispute the individual-factor strength.
limitations: US factors from 1964 on, gross of costs, factor portfolios rather than composite weights inside one book; our inputs are 22 correlated slow signals over 2017-2026.
